HUD, UI & Sounds
Cleaned up HUD (removed shake/scale animations, fixed layouts).

Fixed multiple bugs: holo shield issues, restart after game over, weapon switching while invisible, tutorial teleport bug.

Melee made snappier, laser beam no longer uses physics, anomalies adjusted (removed one per round).

Performance optimization.

Fixed Klaus alternative shooting. Now feels like a proper shotgun.



Changes are now in the playtest branch. Check them out and let me know what you think!

notes.title: Playtest Update: New version is playable
notes.notes:
Things that are added in this version:
Added save/load system. Run progress can be saved and restored now. To save, player has to have enough Save points. Those can be exchanged for scorepoints (7K for each save point).  1 save point = 1 save. Once saved, player can always restart the run from that save point.



Freeplay is available again. All levels discovered in Run mode are playable here.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/3a7308fa6157f705e309b65bf13f08bae4a15da8.png"]

5th level added and glide terrain added. Looks like this. When stepped on, the player gets some inertia. Simulates glidable surface. Affects only player at this moment.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/3614a242852a48be10ad1dc0ba178d91204cc852.png"]

Enabled ReMaze anomaly. Only enabled in 5th level for now. This one randomly repositions level obstacles. 

Added "Synergy" concept. +1 pilot ability use (for September and Meg) for every mech upgrade. So a mech that is evolved to the first state can mark up to 2 targets for rocket and landmine. Second state 3 marks, third state 4 marks. The BX08 ability works a bit differently though. Synergy increases its duration (and thus also distance), not the amount of uses.

Some tweaks in shooting and projectile physics.



Changes are now available in the playtest branch. Feel free to check it out!

In this update, I’ll introduce the second Mech currently available in the playtest version - Klaus.

Playstyle-wise, Klaus is slower than Agamemnon, with less mobility. It's more durable though because of its Action, and thus it's better at holding positions.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/5c9d2079bd2ea82a8a0d899f1783382e597f0964.png"]
Action – Invincibility


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/ec46b123c3ae590c40872d4c2dcbdfa3608f478d.png"]

Becomes immune to all damage for 2 seconds. While invincible, all projectile damage received is directly converted into Energy.

Klaus can thus engage in heavy combat or disengage when overwhelmed.


Alternative Fire – Shotgun


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/84f4766f3e5eefbb6e003d9c32901e2401529172.png"]

One-shots multiple enemies. Especially effective in close combat and against large groups.



The playtest - it's currently open and contains all three pilots and two mechs, including Klaus.

notes.title: Dev Update: Combat Roles Explained
notes.notes:
What to Choose, and Why?

Before starting any run, the player chooses a Mech and a Pilot. The default combo is Agamemnon (Mech) and September (Pilot).

You're free to choose any Mech and pair it with any Pilot.
So—how are they different, and how does your choice affect the game?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/39ae9728323cfbb03ffbf4ef4efbd61dc6848d2b.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/39bd37cc7ff10eec8cfee67b97a7e6a25e0a2e4c.png

Mechs and Pilots

Every Mech and Pilot has a unique ability that defines the playstyle of the unit.
In addition, each Mech comes with its own alternative fire mode.

Here is the default combo as an example.

Agamemnon (Mech)
Ability: Dash

Agamemnon can dash for 3 seconds, significantly increasing speed and destroying everything it touches (except enemy projectiles). It’s highly agile—great for repositioning on the grid, quick retreats, grabbing power-ups, getting to the base, or digging into the environment. And of course, it can chain killstreaks easily by wiping out enemies mid-dash. Simple to use and fast-paced.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/bde25fbcfc2bba6b0e9b673ffdf1bdb5dcde1fed.png

September (Pilot)
Ability: Air Strike

The player marks a target area and calls in an air strike. A projectile hits that exact spot, one-shotting everything, including environmental obstacles.

This ability is different in that it affects the map and enemies, rather than the Mech itself.
But there's a risk: during the targeting process, the Mech becomes inactive—you can't move or react.
This means you’re vulnerable while using it, and it demands a bit of planning and awareness.
Best used from cover—or even better, in co-op when your teammate can protect you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/3e782243e83bc2931f210db68953be6f937a9e09.png

Customization = Gameplay Variety
Mixing Mechs and Pilots changes how the game plays. Some are better for pushing, others for holding back or reacting to what’s happening. It gets especially interesting in co-op, where each player can pick a combo that either supports—or competes with—the other. 

Let’s say we choose a Mech—Kateg. Its ability is invincibility mode, which absorbs all incoming damage and transforms it into energy. Its alt fire is a shotgun, allowing it to channel that energy into short-range bursts—perfect for holding ground temporarily.

As a Pilot, we pick BX08, who can summon portals to redirect enemies or create shortcuts back to the base. This combo allows us to engage in combat briefly, then retreat quickly. Alternatively, we can teleport enemies to a specific location—setting up an ambush right where we want it.

Alternative Fire Modes
Each Mech has a unique alt-fire mode. After collecting enough energy, the player can activate it.

Agamemnon’s alt fire is a quick shot mode that makes bullets hit almost instantly, allowing precise attacks—perfect for hit-and-run tactics.

Here a few rules about alt fire mode:


 Alt-fire attacks consume energy.
 When energy runs out, you return to normal fire.
 You can switch back to normal mode manually at any time.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/f539e7cddf7bb97a695cce76ecca64b1d7bbad3a.png

Limited Usage & Action Points
Each ability use costs 1 action point. These points can be collected during levels or bought between rounds using score points. So, abilities can’t be spammed.

Also, there’s a maximum number of ability uses you can hold. You start with 3 (current)/3 (max) for both Mech and Pilot. You can upgrade this limit between rounds with score points as well.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/0d40b90575a733760ee683c257b9c49698bb1af4.png

That’s about it!
If you liked what you read, check out my previous article on the level grid and obstacles, and of course—try the demo!

notes.title: Dev Update: Environment Mechanics Explained
notes.notes:
Environmental Gameplay – What to Do About It?

The environment in every level is interactable—it's one of the game’s core features. Here's a quick overview of the current state and what the player can do with it.

Grid

First, there's the tile grid, which has a fixed size of 15x13 tiles. The player can move freely in all four directions (up, down, left, right), but not diagonally. Enemies, however, can move diagonally under certain circumstances. The grid always fits the screen, giving the player a full view of what’s going on at every moment

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/611f2770ad8153e49fa17b41462ff0b2d13c4bf6.png

Obstacles

Obstacles form the core of the level environment. They're blocks of different heights placed on the grid to create a maze-like layout.The player must use this maze to their advantage—whether it's for cover, flanking, or escaping danger. Most of these blocks can be destroyed by the player, enemies, or external factors.

Currently, there are three types:

Normal Obstacle (Green) – Destructible. One hit destroys part of the block. Depending on the obstacle’s height, two hits might be needed.
Concrete Obstacle (Gray) – Sometimes destructible. The player can only destroy it in their third evolution form or with an operator ability. Anomalies can also break it.
Power Field – Not destructible (for now). It’s a force field that blocks everything except projectiles. It also slows projectiles down.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/67ec2e84792169320224016954b3c15b9a3373f0.png


Other Environmental Elements
[olist]
Fog – Covers parts of the level and limits visibility. The player needs to be cautious when moving into fog-covered zones.
Pushing Tiles – Step on one, and it pushes the player in a specific direction.
[/olist]
These features make up the current state of the environment.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/1dcafee2fa2bdd3a3d630dcc93f67dda9c8c832f.png

All combined level looks like this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/d3af73766c42488dff7b6f8488af7c12235745a2.png

or this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/303fb930be22bf1d1e47a30960c1285a46ddc69f.png

Why Is the Environment Important?

Navigating the environment and making decisions based on the level’s layout is crucial.
It provides cover and opens up opportunities for tactical plays—like hiding, flanking, or ganking your enemies.

But the environment won’t stay intact. Obstacles can and will be destroyed—by enemies, anomalies, or even the player. When that happens, cover disappears, and the chances of survival drop. Without protection, the player risks being overwhelmed.

To make things even more dynamic, some elements can reshape the level during combat—adding new structures or modifying existing ones. So every level is constantly changing.

The player can’t just run from danger—they have to adapt and respond quickly.
Fast decision-making becomes critical, especially as the level gets more chaotic and intense over time.

notes.title: Version 0.2.1 is out!
notes.notes:
Added countdowns for all power-ups. It’s now much easier to assess the risk of running across the battlefield to grab them.

Changed how the operator ability works:


 The player holds E (1 second).
 A marker is spawned.
 The player selects a point on the battlefield and presses E.
 Projectiles strike the selected location.


It’s now much more usable.
The player has unlimited time to choose the target, allowing them to find an optimal spot and 'snipe' multiple enemies at once. 
However, the player remains fully vulnerable during targeting since movement is disabled, making pacing and timing crucial.

Added support for multiple new languages.

Implemented custom font-per-language mapping. The built-in fallback system was insufficient, especially for seven languages.

Fixed a bug where the player's speed was constantly decreasing in an edge case (when just revived while an anomaly was activated).
Fixed a bug where five enemies were summoned mid-battle due to a power-down.

Properly tested Nintendo Switch controller support—works as expected (wired version only).

notes.title: Version 0.1.6 released
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.6 Released!

Additions:
[olist]

 Energy Gathering / Energy Levels
Players can now gather energy from destroyed enemies and power-ups. After destroying an enemy or collecting a power-up, particles will remain gatherable for a limited time. If the player picks them up, the energy level increases. Gathering energy unlocks features like an alternative weapon mode and awards extra points. The energy level resets at the start of each round.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/e14691133671220be53c7a5eb99d8129dba457ec.png

2. Alternative Weapon Mode
When a player gathers enough energy, an alternative weapon mode can be activated. Once activated, the energy level decreases at a predefined rate (10 energy per second). When energy runs out, the weapon switches back to its normal mode. Players can pick up more energy while in the alternative mode to extend its duration. Each mech has a unique alternative weapon mode.

3. Shield Status Indicator
A new indicator has been added to display shield status.

4. New Trailer is released!

Major Bug Fixes:

1. Fixed an issue where the player was invisible while using the operator ability.
2. Navigation for "Restart" and "Go to Menu" is now fixed on the Level Summary screen (Freerun mode).
3. Levels from Run mode are now properly registered as playable in Freerun mode.
4. Fine-tuned collision detection when players destroy the environment.
5. Resolved messaging issues in the tutorial.


In Progress (Not Included in This Release):
1. A third enemy type.
2. A second anomaly.
3. Power-downs that enemies can pick up.

notes.title: Version 0.1.05 released
notes.notes:
Hi there! This one is quite minor. I am currently working on expanding and refactoring the point registration system.
It will reward players for actions like picking up power-ups, completing a round without dying, etc.
I'm also working on a new trailer because the game looks quite different since the last one.
In the meantime, I’ve added some visual improvements:

1. Added a prewarm state – the player is no longer just standing at the start of the round but has a nice walkout (or jump off) animation.
2. Visual effect after picking up a power-up. The power-up now explodes, and after a short delay, the particles are pulled toward the player—a nice little visual cue that confirms the pickup.
3. Added electricity sparks on projectile collision.
4. Added flake particles to the first level.
5. The UI HUD is now a bit more dynamic. It reacts to certain level events and has a nice appearance effect.


That’s about it for this release! Stay tuned!

notes.title: Version 0.1.04 released
notes.notes:
Time for a new update!
Meet BX08 - Second Playable Pilot!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/d245d72176ec40e0f0f567350f5e3139070653c6.png


I was thinking about implementing an ability that won’t directly deal damage or influence enemies, but rather something that enables tactics and controls the flow of the match (e.g. retreating, redirecting enemies, setting up traps).

Here’s how it works:

1. The pilot selects the locations for the first and second teleport and summons them.
2. Afterward, the teleports become connected, so anything that enters one comes out the other (and vice versa).
3. This enables interesting tactics, like placing a teleport near enemies and waiting by the second, or even shooting through the teleport.
4. The initial direction of a projectile is preserved after teleportation. So, if you stand directly in front of the teleport, the projectile will continue moving forward after it teleports.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/3ee29a584959e41cc733196d90a54f14023c45a5.png

5. The same applies for back, right, and left directions. This works for everything, including the first pilot’s ability (controllable projectile), which can be nicely combined in co-op play.
6. As with every pilot ability, it temporarily disables the mech, making it extra vulnerable. Therefore, it should be used from a safe spot (though "safe" is subjective—there are no safe spots in Decurion!).

The second update in this build is the Shield. I designed it to give players a better chance of surviving tough situations, but it requires some skill.
The shield summons immediately and will absorb one projectile, after which it disappears and becomes available again after a short cooldown.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/fcd56fa754d9d909881de7998a13c4c818cd1d38.png

It costs nothing, works quickly, and allows players to take extra risks and escape dangerous situations unharmed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44826505/e299ed1d6c4a3688fa1d0ab772b8785c0aa2b0b6.png

If activated right before impact, the shield will deflect the projectile back to the enemy. This only works against projectiles!

That’s all for this update! Stay tuned!
